scope: Non-archive topic map for the requested asymptotic, q-analog, combinatorial-sequence and interpolated-inverse reading list. Not a complete selection manifest and not an independent mathematical validation.
archive_policy: Exclude all docs/archive, following latest user instruction. Earlier archive review is unused.
important_findings: The two transseries volumes are the central combinatorial reading list.
A dedicated real-argument Fibonacci inverse chapter is present.
Bell-number forward all-order saddle expansions and Fubini convergent pole expansions are present. No dedicated Bell-number interpolant inverse was located.
q-analog inverse coverage is substantial in the Combinatorial Transseries Inverses volume and the q-Pochhammer/q-Binomial monograph.
Exact extraction companions are labeled separately from asymptotic articles.

caveats: The Bell-number chapter supplies forward saddle expansions, not an identified Bell-number interpolant inverse.
The Fibonacci inverse expansion is convergent, with log-periodic sectors.
Interpolation choices, parity branches, and discrete threshold inverses are distinguished in the source.
The Bell chapter expressly labels nonprincipal complex-saddle sectors as formal and does not determine Stokes multipliers.

readingOrder.scopeAndStatus: The dedicated Fibonacci chapter specifies the interpolation and branches, derives a closed inverse coefficient formula, and organizes the real correction terms into log-periodic sectors. The source states convergence and a truncation error bound; this is a functional inverse of that specified interpolation.

readingOrder.title: Bell numbers: Lambert saddle and forward all-order expansions
readingOrder.scopeAndStatus: The main volume gives Bell-number forward saddle expansions and a ranked logarithmic organization. No dedicated inverse of a Bell-number interpolant was located. Nonprincipal complex-saddle sectors are explicitly formal; the coefficient-calculus volume separately withdraws its former refined Moser-Wyman claim while retaining leading and logarithmic results.

evidence.source: the third family lying beyond every power of $L^{-1}$ relative to the first

readingOrder.title: Fubini numbers: ordered Bell numbers and a convergent pole transseries
readingOrder.scopeAndStatus: The exponential generating function produces an exact pole-lattice expansion with oscillatory exponential corrections and certified truncation. This is forward sequence coverage; it should not be presented as a Bell-number interpolation inverse.

evidence.source: \chapter{The Fubini numbers: an exact pole lattice}

readingOrder.title: Rooted trees: singularity transfer and asymptotic inversion
readingOrder.scopeAndStatus: The Butcher-Polya chapter develops the Otter-singularity Puiseux expansion, transfers it to all-order rooted-tree coefficient asymptotics, and constructs an inverse with a Lambert carrier and exponentially small sectors.

evidence.source: \section{The Puiseux expansion at the Otter singularity}

readingOrder.title: Partitions: Rademacher sectors and arithmetic inverse transseries
readingOrder.scopeAndStatus: The partition chapter organizes Rademacher terms into forward arithmetic sectors, then gives the dominant Lambert inverse and its subdominant corrections. It distinguishes the chosen continuous inverse from threshold recovery of the discrete sequence.

evidence.source: \section{Rademacher's formula in exact transseries normal form}
\section{The Lambert core and the algebraic inverse}\label{p3:sec:lambert}

readingOrder.title: Factorial families: double factorial, multifactorials, swing factorial and subfactorial
readingOrder.scopeAndStatus: Factorial-scale sequence chapters treat algebraic and exponentially small inverse corrections. Parity branches and the interpolation choice are essential; the swing-factorial sequence is not eventually monotone, so a single unqualified inverse would be misleading.

readingOrder.title: Catalan and balanced gamma-quotient families
readingOrder.scopeAndStatus: A common gamma-quotient engine gives forward expansions and all-order inverse corrections for Catalan, Fuss-Catalan, central multinomial and related families. The coefficient-calculus volume supplies an additional explicit Catalan forward expansion.

evidence.source: \chapter{The gamma-quotient engine and the balanced families}

readingOrder.title: Stirling and Eulerian columns
readingOrder.scopeAndStatus: Fixed columns lead to distinct multiexponential or logarithmic structures. The treatment includes second-kind Stirling numbers and surjections, Eulerian columns, and first-kind Stirling numbers with nested-log inverse corrections; these are not interchangeable asymptotic regimes.

evidence.source: \section{Stirling numbers of the second kind and surjections}
\section{Unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind}

readingOrder.title: Moment sequences, involutions and alternating permutations
readingOrder.scopeAndStatus: Endpoint extraction covers Motzkin, trinomial, Delannoy and Schroder families. Involutions require two saddles and a stretched-exponential inverse with nonbounded drift. Alternating permutations use parity-resolved gamma blocks and exponentially small sectors.

readingOrder.title: Graphs, necklaces, Lyndon words and irreducible polynomials
readingOrder.scopeAndStatus: Connected labelled graphs have quadratic growth phases with successive exponential layers. Divisor-sum families require arithmetic sectors and explicitly defined finite-cutoff interpolations; the volume also separates these inverses from certified discrete threshold recovery.

readingOrder.title: q-factorials, Gaussian binomials and finite-field enumeration inverses
readingOrder.scopeAndStatus: The q-product part covers general linear groups, flags, q-factorials, Gaussian binomials, q-Catalan numbers and classical-group orders. It gives functional inverse corrections and convergent fixed-rank inverse Puiseux series. A q-factorial functional inverse is explicitly distinguished from its reciprocal.

evidence.source: Here the notation on the left means the inverse of the interpolation just defined, not the reciprocal of a factorial.
\chapter{$q$-Catalan numbers and the symplectic and unitary orders}

readingOrder.title: Galois theta inverses and the singular q-to-one crossover
readingOrder.scopeAndStatus: Galois-number inverses are organized on residue sheets with theta coefficients. The separate q-to-one analysis gives uniform dilogarithmic forward expansions and asymptotic inverse crossover corrections. This is a continuous analytic-base limit, not finite-field orders tending to one; crossover convergence is not claimed.

evidence.source: \section{An all-order dilogarithmic expansion of the tail}

\eqref{t3:eq:general-derivative}. At each fixed $m$, only finitely many $E_j$ occur. Each $c_m$ is a polynomial in $L_h$ of degree at most $m$, with smooth coefficients in $\tau_*$. The finite-order expansions are asymptotic with remainders controlled by the preceding propositions; no convergence assertion is made for this Bernoulli-based expansion in $h$.

readingOrder.title: Related q coefficient and inverse machinery
readingOrder.scopeAndStatus: Gaussian Coefficient Calculus separates exact fixed-rank, convergent fixed-base bulk, and uniform Poincare double-scaling expansions. The q-Pochhammer monograph supplies complementary large-target product inverses, q-to-one base inverses and inverse q-special functions; the dedicated q reading list gives the fuller branch-aware route.

readingOrder.title: Exact dyadic extraction companions
readingOrder.scopeAndStatus: These companions explain exact finite-spline and deconvolution identities connected to asymptotic prefix laws and Gaussian-binomial coefficient rows. Their principal recovery statements are exact, including zero remainder; they are not Bell/Fibonacci interpolation inverse articles or generic q-to-one asymptotic claims.
